messages:
Alex: Quick thread — decision needed on runtime contract strictness vs policy DSL hygiene. We just hit a regression where the runtime silently tolerated an extra field and routing behaved incorrectly.
Maria: Can you paste the failing example?
Alex: Here — customer policy payload we accepted:
```
{
  "route": "edge-eu",
  "priority": 10,
  "deprecated_affinity": true, // legacy field
  "constraints": {"latency_ms": 200}
}
```
Runtime ignored deprecated_affinity and picked a bucket that violated their expectations.
Zheng: Two broad options: (A) strict validation at ingestion (reject policies that contain unknown/deprecated fields), or (B) soft validation + linter + telemetry that warns but still accepts.
Casey: We have Dedicated customers with hundreds of policies they can’t update quickly. Rejecting will cause support load. Prefer an opt-in enforcement where tenants can flip a flag to opt into strict mode.
Alex: My proposal: add a policy_version field and a migration path. New ingestion validates strictly for policy_version >= 2. For older policies we run a compatibility shim that maps deprecated fields to the new shape where safe, and emits a warning.
Jordan: What about runtime cost? We already do some shape checks in hot path. If we add validation at runtime that could add latency.
Alex: Validation happens at ingestion only. Runtime will do minimal presence checks for fields that affect fast-path decisions (e.g., affinity token, preemptive_window). Heavy schema validation stays offline. So runtime cost is negligible.
ops-bot: deploy-staging: validation-service v0.9 pushed to staging; smoke tests started.
Maria: Rollout plan suggestion: feature-flagged ingestion validator -> console/CLI linter that previews fixes -> canary 5% tenants with strict=true -> increase after no regressions 1 week.
Zheng: Also add a migration linter rule set in the Console that can auto-apply safe mappings (e.g., deprecated_affinity -> affinity_mode: "legacy"). Provide a one-click bulk migrate.
Casey: We should also publish a compat table in docs and include an acceptance test matrix: (policy_version, runtime_version) -> expected behavior. That will help SRE and CS.
Alex: Timeline rough: 2w for linter + ingestion validation code, 1w for Console UX + bulk migrate, 2w canary + bake. We can parallelize tests.
Jordan: :thumbsup: If we go this route we should also add a telemetry event that surfaces which tenants are still on legacy mappings so PM/CS can nudge them.
Alex: Agreed. Action items: (1) Zheng + Maria own linter + mappings list, (2) Casey owns compat test matrix, (3) Alex owns ingestion validator and policy_version bump RFC, (4) Ops monitors canary and telemetry.
Maria: Noted. I'll create the RFC doc and a quick checklist for rollout tomorrow.
Casey: Will start drafting tests and the compat table.
Alex: Thanks — we’ll sync in architecture sync if anything blocks.
